skills.does: Work out how many days you kept a habit, as a percentage of the days in the period.
examples: how often did I keep this habit
what is my completion rate this week

skills.does: Rank tasks by importance, urgency and how much effort they take.
Build a rota that shares tasks evenly between people over several rounds.
examples: make a rota for these chores
rotate two jobs between two people
share one task between three people

skills.does: Count the days done in a row from a list of dates — the current and longest streak.
examples: what is my current run of days

skills.does: Lay tasks out as time blocks through the day, with breaks between them.
examples: schedule these tasks back to back

skills.does: Look up an airport by its IATA code, or find the airports serving a city.
Look up a country's capital city, ISO codes, currency and international dialling code.
examples: what is the capital of Switzerland

skills.does: Look up what a currency code stands for — its name, symbol and how many decimal places it uses.
Look up what a two-letter language code stands for, or find the code for a language — ISO 639-1.
examples: what is the code for Portuguese

skills.does: Look up a chemical element — magnesium, Mg, or atomic number 12 — for its symbol, mass and group.
examples: what is the atomic weight of carbon

skills.does: Find which country an international dialling code belongs to, or the code for a country.
examples: what is the dialling code for India

skills.does: Find the current time and UTC offset in a time zone.
examples: what time is it in Asia/Tokyo
what is the utc offset in New York

skills.does: Look up a US state by name or postal abbreviation.
examples: what is the capital of California

skills.does: Look up a short factual answer on the web, with the page it came from.
examples: who is the governor of Maryland
what is the James Webb Space Telescope

skills.does: Search the web and get back the matching pages, with links.
examples: search the web for the Antikythera mechanism

skills.does: Measure how strongly two sets of numbers move together, as a correlation coefficient.
examples: how correlated are these two series
correlation between hours studied and score

skills.does: Build a running total as you go, showing the sum after each number.
examples: cumulative sum of my monthly savings

skills.does: Summarise a list of numbers — its mean, median, mode, minimum, maximum, range and spread.
Spot the values sitting way off from the rest of a set.
examples: find the outliers in these numbers

skills.does: Bucket numbers into a number of equal-width ranges and count how many fall in each.
examples: histogram of these scores in 4 bins
distribution of these ages in 3 bins

skills.does: Fit a straight line through a set of points and give its slope, intercept and fit.
examples: fit a line through these points
trend line for these sales figures

skills.does: Smooth a series of numbers by averaging over a sliding window.
examples: 3 point moving average of these numbers
smooth these sales figures over 4 months
moving average of a noisy series

skills.does: Find the value at a given percentile in a set of numbers.
examples: what is the 90th percentile of these response times

skills.does: Split a set of numbers into quartiles and give the interquartile range.
Put numbers in order and give each its rank position.
Average a set of values where some count for more than others.
examples: weighted average of 80 and 90 where the second counts double
weighted average where all weights are equal

skills.does: Standardise a set of numbers — how many standard deviations each value sits from the mean.
examples: how unusual is each of these

skills.does: Work out the typical word size in a text — its average word length.
examples: average word length of this sentence
how long are the words on average

skills.does: Strip the timestamps, cue numbers and repeated speaker labels out of an auto-generated transcript, rejoin the sentences its captions cut in half, and drop the stutters and filler words.
examples: strip the timestamps out of this transcript
clean up this auto generated transcript
tidy this srt subtitle file into readable text

skills.does: Change text to another capitalisation — title case, upper, lower, camelCase, snake_case.
examples: make this title case: the lord of the rings

skills.does: Count the characters in a text — with spaces, without spaces, and how many are letters or digits.
examples: character count with spaces and without

skills.does: Count the lines in a block of text, separating blank lines from lines with content.
examples: count lines including the blank ones
line count of a single line

skills.does: Count how many times one word or phrase repeats inside a text.
examples: how many times does "the" appear in this
count how often "error" shows up in the log

skills.does: Count the sentences in a text, and the average sentence length.
examples: sentence count with an abbreviation in it

skills.does: Measure how long a piece of text is: its total words, characters, sentences and paragraphs.
examples: how many words is this paragraph
word count for a two sentence note
count the words in my two paragraphs

skills.does: Guess which language a piece of text is written in.
examples: identify the language of this sentence
which language is this written in

skills.does: Find phrases a piece of text repeats.
examples: check for repeated phrases of two words

skills.does: Compare two versions of a text and show what was added and removed, by line or by word.
examples: show me the line by line changes
diff these two paragraphs by word
compare the old and new list

skills.does: Make text safe to drop into HTML, turning angle brackets and ampersands into entities — or turn escaped ones back.
